args:
{"generate": {"pageType": "software", "url": "https://example.com/pricing", "title": "Ledgerline pricing | Example Co.", "description": "Month-end close for multi-entity finance teams, from $59 a month.", "image": "https://example.com/og.png", "siteName": "Example Co.", "software": {"name": "Ledgerline", "applicationCategory": "BusinessApplication", "operatingSystem": "Web", "price": "59", "priceCurrency": "usd", "ratingValue": "4.8", "ratingCount": "120"}, "breadcrumbs": [{"name": "Home", "url": "https://example.com/"}, {"name": "Pricing"}], "llms": {"summary": "Month-end close software for multi-entity finance teams.", "sections": [{"title": "Docs", "links": [{"title": "Pricing", "url": "https://example.com/pricing", "note": "plans and prices"}]}]}, "html": "

Ledgerline pricing

Home / Pricing

Team plan: $59 per month. Rated 4.8 from 120 reviews.

"}, "today": "2026-10-29"}
stdout: AAJ - STRUCTURED DATA, META TAGS AND LLMS.TXT (software page)
READY TO PUBLISH - No broken or unsupported markup found for SoftwareApplication, and what it marks up appears in the page text.
<meta name="description" content="Month-end close for multi-entity finance teams, from $59 a month.">
<meta property="og:description" content="Month-end close for multi-entity finance teams, from $59 a month.">
> Month-end close software for multi-entity finance teams.

i  [SoftwareApplication] A rating of 4.8 from 120 ratings was included because you entered it. Google: "Don't mark up content that is not visible to readers of the page." Show the same rating and count on the page.
i  [meta] The twitter:card tag is AAJ's addition, not from the sources cited here: it asks X for a large-image link card. Remove it if you don't need it.
i  [llms.txt] The llms.txt H1 was set to "Example Co.". It describes the whole site, so enter another name if that isn't right.

i  [llms.txt] llms.txt is a proposed format, not a standard: an H1 with the site name (the only required section), an optional summary in a blockquote, then H2 sections of links. Save it at /llms.txt.

i  [llms.txt] Google says: "You don't need to create new machine readable files, AI text files, or markup to appear in these features" (AI Overviews and AI Mode). So llms.txt is optional, and not a lever for Google.

i  [-] Google says there is "no special schema.org structured data" needed for AI Overviews or AI Mode, and lists "making sure your structured data matches the visible text on the page" among the fundamentals.
